notes: AN ADVANCE WHOSE CHEQUE NEVER REACHED THE REGISTER IS NOW NAMED. Issuing an advance does two things: it posts the entry to the ledger, and it puts the cheque on the register. If the second one did not finish — the app was closed, the machine slept, something interrupted it — the books were left in a state nothing could see. The receivable and the general ledger agree with each other, so every balance check stayed quiet, and the only symptom was a bank reconciliation that would not come out, with no row anywhere explaining why. The difference had to be forced by hand. The health check now reads staff advances the way it has read payments since August: an advance whose own record NAMES a cheque, on a posted entry, with no row on the register, is reported by name and amount together with what to do about it. It stays silent where nothing is wrong — an advance recorded without a cheque number, a draft that has not paid anybody, and an advance that has been reversed are all left alone, because a warning that fires when nothing is wrong is worse than no warning at all. ALSO IN THIS BUILD, FROM 0.6.92: VAT — THE WHOLE CHARGE IS RECLAIMABLE FROM 2026. The Value Added Tax Act, 2025 (Act 1151) took effect on 1 January 2026. It abolished the COVID-19 levy, recoupled the NHIL and the GETFund levy to the VAT base, and made both deductible as input tax — they were not before. A VAT-registered organisation now reclaims the whole charge on a purchase rather than fifteen points of it. YOUR OLDER RECORDS ARE NOT RESTATED: which treatment applies is decided by the date on the document, so a bill dated before 2026 keeps exactly the treatment it was entered under and nothing already in your books moves.
